newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares extend losses, gains not seen.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares extend losses, gains not seen.

text.p: * Lithuanian shares extended recent losses on Tuesday and dealers did not expect activity to pick up soon.
* The official list index, which tracks the bourse's four leading blue chip stocks, fell 20.07 points to 906.56.
* The Litin A index, which covers the bourse's 43 most active shares, lost 55.12 points to close at 2,275.29.
* Overall central market volume was 1.18 million litas while block trade volume reached 910,500 litas.
* Lithuanian Gas returned to the market after its shareholders' meeting and promptly shed nine percent, falling to 1.82 litas to 2.00 litas.
* No bank shares gained though Hermis Bank was relatively active in trade of 554,400 litas at the unchanged price of 175.00 litas.
Lithuanian shares extended their losses on Tuesday and dealers said that gains were not on the immediate horizon.

"We only have a few local investors right now and a few orders from the Nordic countries...the big investors are still examining the market and haven't come yet," said Kestutis Kupsys, a broker with Mendes Prior Europe.
Dealers said foreign investors, who have been reassured that the government will not devalue the litas for some time, seemed more interested in debt at the moment.
Tuesday's primary auction for 50 million litas worth of 179-day Treasury bills attracted almost 140 million litas in bids.

The session's losers included Lithuanian Gas, which returned to the market after its shareholders' meeting and promptly lost nine percent, easing to 1.82 litas from 2.00 in trade of just under 7,000 litas.
The company reported losses for 1996 of 15.98 million litas but dealers said it still looked undervalued and had lots of room to grow.
No banking shares gained though Hermis Bank shares were in relative demand, turning over 554,400 litas at the unchanged price of 175.00 litas.
Siauliu Bank slid for the third straight seesion after rapidly gaining last week on Hermis Bank's announcement that it planned to acquire a 51 percent stake.
It eased to 82.00 litas from 90.00 in trade of 11,726 litas.
Siauliu Bank said on Tuesday that its current shareholders would probably be hesitant to sell to Hermis Bank, casting doubt on the project.
